motion.name: ease-out

motion.name: scroll-linear
motion.value: linear, animation-fill-mode: both, on view() or a named view-timeline

motion.name: scroll-longhands
motion.value: animation-name / animation-timing-function / animation-fill-mode / animation-timeline / animation-range as separate declarations

motion.name: scroll-gate
motion.value: @supports (animation-timeline: view()) and @media (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference)

narrative.overview:
A personal page built the way Apple builds a product page, with Stripe's finish: one idea per section, big confident type, real media, and scroll moments that carry the story. Every section is a full-width band on one of three grounds (white, Apple grey, true black), with content on a 1080px column that images deliberately break: they bleed off a viewport edge or cross a section edge, and the copy alternates sides. Density is low on purpose. A section holds a headline, a lead, and at most one piece of media or one pair of actions.

Papaya is the only colour that isn't a neutral. It appears as the pill button, the text links, the drawn lines (the Sochi trace, the MS wave), the hero's drifting gradient band, and the full-bleed swatch band. Everything else is ink on paper or paper on black. Depth comes from the ground changing, not from shadows.

Motion is scroll-driven CSS. One-time reveals bring text, the team tile and the speedmark in as they enter view. Scroll-driven CSS lights words, drifts the rain, draws lines and fills a reading-progress line. Reduced motion and browsers without `animation-timeline` get the finished state, never an empty one.
keyCharacteristics: Three section grounds: white, Apple grey, black. The nav follows them.
One accent, papaya, used for actions and drawn lines.
Mona Sans only, weights 500 to 700, with tight tracking on display sizes.
Centred, single-column sections with generous vertical padding.
Real photographs in 28px-rounded frames or full-bleed bands, always credited.
Scroll-driven CSS motion whose resting state is the finished state.

rules.name: The One Orange Rule
rules.body: Papaya is the only accent. It marks things you can act on, and lines that tell the story. Nothing decorative is papaya except the hero band and the swatch band, and each appears once.

rules.name: The Three Grounds Rule
rules.body: Every section sits on #ffffff, #f5f5f7 or #000000. Ground changes are the section breaks; no borders, cards or tinted panels stand in for them. The one exception is a photo band, where the photograph is the ground.

rules.name: The Papaya-As-Text Rule
rules.body: Text in papaya uses #a94f00 on light grounds and #ff9a3d on black. Raw #ff8000 is for fills and strokes only.

rules.name: The One Family Rule
rules.body: Mona Sans only. Hierarchy comes from size, weight (500, 560, 600, 650, 700) and tracking, never from a second typeface.

rules.name: The Tight Display Rule
rules.body: The bigger the type, the tighter the tracking: -0.04em at display, -0.035em at headline and statement, -0.025em at title, about -0.01em at body.

rules.name: The Sentence Case Rule
rules.body: No uppercase, no letter-spaced small labels, and no small line above a headline. A headline introduces itself.

rules.name: The No-Shadow Rule
rules.body: Nothing floats. If something needs separating, change the ground, add a 1px hairline, or use a zero-offset ring.

dos: Do put every section on #ffffff, #f5f5f7 or #000000, and add the `.dark` class to black sections so the nav turns dark over them.
Do pair one papaya pill with one chevron text link in a centred action row.
Do use #a94f00 for papaya text on light grounds and #ff9a3d on black.
Do write scroll-driven animations as longhands inside `@supports (animation-timeline: view())` and `prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference`, with the finished state as the default.

Do source photographs from Pixabay through `scripts/fetch-pixabay.mjs` (IDs in `scripts/pixabay.json`). Commit them to `src/assets/pixabay/`, serve them through Astro's `Picture` (avif and webp at 640, 960 and 1280 widths), and credit each one both under the image and in the footer from `credits.json`.
Do keep images at or below the 1280px the standard Pixabay key returns. Size frames and `sizes` attributes so a 1280px source is not stretched past it.
Do keep tap targets at 2.75rem or more, and give every drawn chart a prose equivalent for screen readers.
donts: Don't use drop shadows, cards or tinted panels. Separate with the ground, a 1px hairline or a zero-offset ring.
Don't add a second accent colour. Ribbon orange lives only in the swatch band.
Don't use raw #ff8000 for small text on white or grey.
Don't use the `animation` shorthand for a scroll-driven animation.
Don't hotlink Pixabay images or ship the API key. The key stays in `.env`.
Don't set labels in uppercase or tracked small caps, and don't put a small label line above a headline.
Don't repeat the hero gradient band or the swatch band. Each is used once.
Don't introduce a second typeface or an icon font. Icons are inline Lucide SVGs.

patchr.note: A second, separate visual world. Its frontmatter tokens are the patchr- keys in DESIGN.md. The top-level extensions, components and narrative belong to the personal site and do not apply here; the shared reveal system (src/styles/reveal.css, src/scripts/reveal.ts) is the only shared code.

narrative.overview:
This is the Discord-bot landing page that server owners already know from MEE6, YAGPDB and Carl.gg: a hero with Add to Discord, feature rows proven by Discord product shots, how it works, limits, commands, FAQ, one drenched call-to-action band, and a legal footer. It is built with the personal site's Apple and Stripe finish, in Patchr's own brand kit (`brand/BRAND.md`). The page starts dark, because visitors arrive from Discord's dark UI. It opens on deep ink, moves through light white and mist feature sections, returns to deep ink for How it works, and ends on the pink band.

The proof is the product itself. Every feature is shown as a Discord screen drawn in HTML, using the layout and strings of Patchr's real renderer. The screens bleed off the viewport edge, opposite the copy. Discord's own greys stay inside those product shots, the way a phone keeps its own screen colours inside a product photo. Pink is the one action colour, and in the brand it means *the newest change*.
keyCharacteristics: Deep ink for dark sections, white or mist for light ones. The nav follows the ground beneath it.
One accent, pink, used for actions, the newest change and drawn lines. Ink text sits on it.
Inter Variable only: 800 for display and headlines with tight tracking, 500 for leads.
Discord product shots that bleed off alternating viewport edges, rounded only on their inner corners.
Add to Discord is the live pink pill, opening Patchr's invite in a new tab, with the support server beside it.
One-time reveals, a floating 3D hero tile, and scroll-drawn pink lines, all with a finished resting state.

rules.name: The Ink-On-Pink Rule
rules.body: Pink is the one action colour. Whatever sits on pink is set in Patchr Ink, never white. White on pink is under 3:1, and ink on pink is above 6:1.

rules.name: The Deep-Pink Text Rule
rules.body: Pink as text on white or mist uses patchr-pink-text. Raw pink is for fills, strokes and text on dark.

rules.name: The Badge-Only Rule
rules.body: Mint and lilac exist only in the Fix and Change badges. They are never a text colour, fill or accent on the page.

rules.name: The Screen-Colours Rule
rules.body: Discord's greys, and the colours of the GitHub release card, appear only inside product shots of those UIs. That means the Discord screens, the /patch modal floating off the second screen, and the source and output cards in How it works. Around them the page stays in Patchr's own palette.

rules.name: The One Family Rule
rules.body: Inter only (plus system mono for commands). Hierarchy comes from size, weight (500, 550, 560, 600, 620, 650, 700, 750, 800) and tracking.

rules.name: The Sentence Case Rule
rules.body: No uppercase labels and no small line above a headline. The one uppercase string is Discord's own APP tag, inside a product shot.

rules.name: The Floating Layer Rule
rules.body: Only a layer that floats over other content gets a soft shadow, and it always comes with a 1px ring. Everything at rest is flat.

rules.name: The One Drench Rule
rules.body: The pink band is the page's one drenched moment: full-bleed pink, ink text, the Patchr mark popping in, a centred headline (max 16ch), and the Add to Discord and ink View code pair. Text selection inverts to ink with pink text. It appears once, just before the footer.

dos: Do put dark sections on patchr-deep, and light sections on white or mist with `.light` (and `.mist`), so the nav follows the ground.
Do set ink text on pink, Deep Pink for pink text on light grounds, and raw pink only for fills, strokes and text on dark.
Do lead every action row with Add to Discord, and link the support server wherever help is offered. Take all three Patchr URLs from src/data/patchr/links.ts.
Do prove features with Discord screens built from Patchr's real renderer layout and strings, bleeding off the edge opposite the copy, rounded only on the inner corners, and captioned as examples.
Do open external links in a new tab with a visually hidden "(opens in a new tab)".
Do write scroll-driven animation as longhands inside both gates, with the finished state as the default.
Do keep tap targets at 2.75rem or more.
donts: Don't put white text on pink.
Don't use mint or lilac outside the Fix and Change badges, or Discord's greys outside a product shot.
Don't bring the personal site's papaya or Mona Sans onto /patchr/, or Patchr's pink and Inter onto the personal pages.
Don't add a second drenched band. The pink CTA band appears once.
Don't add side stripes to cards. The Patch card's accent stripe is the one exception, because it reproduces Discord.
Don't give resting surfaces a drop shadow. Only floating layers get one, always with a 1px ring.
Don't use uppercase or tracked labels, or a small line above a headline.
Don't recolour the Patchr mark's bars or set the wordmark in another font.
